paper_title: Carrier dynamic monitoring of a pi-conjugated polymer: a surface-enhanced Raman scattering method

knowledge_points.content: The conducting polymer poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) can be utilized as a metal-free, pi-conjugated SERS-active substrate for monitoring interfacial carrier dynamics.
knowledge_points.evidence: The conductive polymer poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) is employed as a metal-free SERS substrate. Under different voltage conditions, the SERS performance of the semiconductors’ rectification characteristic is discussed.

knowledge_points.content: The SERS enhancement factor (EF) for a smooth PEDOT:PSS film using methylene blue (MB) as a probe molecule is calculated to be 2.26 x 10^3 based on the peak at 1627 cm^-1.
knowledge_points.evidence: Surprisingly, the enhancement factor (EF) of the PEDOT:PSS film with a root-mean-square (RMS) of 1.81 nm can be up to 2.26 x 10^3... The peak at 1627 cm^-1 for MB is significantly selectively enhanced... it is truly the best choice for evaluating the enhancement factor.

knowledge_points.content: The high enhancement factor in PEDOT:PSS substrates is attributed to pi-electron delocalization and its semimetallic nature, which allows for both chemical enhancement (charge transfer) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) contributions.
knowledge_points.evidence: The main reason for the high EF is pi electron delocalization, which induced the chemical enhancement contribution upon laser excitation... In addition, PEDOT:PSS is also regarded as a semimetallic material, which means that upon laser excitation, a large number of excited-state electrons delocalize and oscillate collectively, which induces enhancement from the SPR contribution.

knowledge_points.content: In a PEDOT:PSS/Methylene Blue (MB) heterojunction, PEDOT:PSS acts as an electron donor (p-type semiconductor) while MB acts as an n-type semiconductor containing electron-withdrawing groups.
knowledge_points.evidence: In fact, PEDOT:PSS acts as an electron donor, and can also be considered a p-type semiconductor; additionally, MB molecules contain electron-withdrawing groups, which can be seen as n-type semiconductors.

knowledge_points.content: Under reverse bias voltage in a polymer-based SERS device, a Raman peak blueshift indicates an increase in carrier density due to accumulation, while a redshift indicates a decrease in carrier density as carriers move directionally under current impulse.
knowledge_points.evidence: When we set the voltage to 0.5 and 1 V, the peak blueshifted and then redshifted with a further increase in voltage. As reported in our previous work, we found that the blueshift and redshift of the peak indicated an increase and decrease in the carrier density, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Treatment of PEDOT:PSS with Hydrochloric acid (HCl) enhances conductivity by reducing the interaction between PEDOT and PSS and facilitating the removal of the poorly conductive PSS component.
knowledge_points.evidence: Jianyong Ouyang’s group reported that HCl treatment is an efficient method to change the conductivity of PEDOT:PSS. After PEDOT:PSS was treated with HCl, the interaction between PEDOT and PSS was lower; moreover, the acid assisted in the removal of poorly conductive PSS.

knowledge_points.content: Molecular coupling between PEDOT:PSS and Methylene Blue (MB) results in an optical absorbance redshift, with the maximum peak shifting from approximately 655 nm to 668 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: the MB molecule has a strong absorption peak at ~655 nm. Both of the above absorption characteristics are observed for the mixture; however, the maximum absorbance peak shifts to ~668 nm due to the coupling of the PEDOT:PSS and MB molecules.

knowledge_points.content: The Raman shift in PEDOT:PSS/MB systems is optimized at an HCl treatment concentration of 0.5 M; higher concentrations lead to corrosion of the PEDOT:PSS layer and the FTO substrate, reducing carrier accumulation.
knowledge_points.evidence: With an HCl concentration of 0.5 M, the value of the Raman shift is maximal... when the concentration of HCl continues to increase, the PEDOT:PSS layer and even FTO will be corroded, which will affect the electron transport process of the entire substrate. Reducing the number of accumulated carriers correspondingly reduces the redshift of the SESR peaks.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) of the PEDOT:PSS SERS substrate reveals an extremely smooth surface with a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 1.81 nm over a 2 x 2 micrometer area.
knowledge_points.evidence: these parameters of a PEDOT:PSS film were obtained by atomic force microscopy (AFM), as shown in Fig. 1(b). The scanning area was 2 x 2 μm^2, and the RMS was 1.81 nm, which indicates that the surface of the PEDOT:PSS film is extremely smooth.

knowledge_points.content: The carrier dynamics of conjugated polymers under static conditions are typically described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) tight-binding model.
knowledge_points.evidence: As usual, under static conditions, the most commonly used microscopic model for the description of the carrier dynamics properties of conjugated polymers is based on the SSH tight-binding model, established by Su, Schrieffer and Heeger.
